translationRepairs: Under Emperor Cheng, Grand General Wang Feng—the Yuan consort's brother—sought to engage Zheng Zizhen with formal honors; Zizhen refused to the last and never took office.
Under Emperor Cheng, Grand General Wang Feng, the emperor's eldest maternal uncle,sought to engage Zheng Zizhen with formal honors; Zizhen refused to the last and never took office.
元舅 means the emperor's eldest maternal uncle; the idiomatic "the Yuan consort's brother" misreads 元 as a name.
Yang Xiong had studied with him in his youth before making a name in the capital; more than once high ministers at court repeated praise of Junping's character.
Yang Xiong had studied with him in his youth before making a name in the capital; more than once he praised Junping's virtue to the worthy men holding office at court.
In 數為朝廷在位賢者稱君平德 the subject is Yang Xiong, who praised Junping to the worthies in office; the idiomatic English wrongly makes the ministers the praisers.
I have read that armies of old marched thirty li a day on the march and at most fifty when the roads were good.
I have read that in antiquity armies marched thirty li a day, and peaceful journeys fifty li.
吉行 means an auspicious (non-military) journey contrasted with 師 (army); "when the roads were good" is not in the source.

If Your Majesty would fix your heart on such things, you would match Yao and Shun in intent and Peng Zu and Prince Qiao in years; a good name would reach the throne above you, blessings would follow in train, and the altars of the state would stand firm.

If Your Majesty would fix your heart on such things, you would match Yao and Shun in intent and Prince Qiao and Master Red Pine in years; a good name would reach the throne above you, blessings would follow in train, and the altars of the state would stand firm.
喬松 names the immortals Wangzi Qiao and Chisongzi (Master Red Pine); Peng Zu is not in the source.

The late emperor was humane and wise; the court still mourns him and has not turned to palace pleasures or hunting in the parks. You should weigh that example day and night and show that you share the same mind.

The emperor is humane and sage; he still longs for the late emperor and has not indulged in palaces, parks or hunting. You should weigh that example day and night and show that you share the same mind.
皇帝 is the reigning Emperor Zhao, the subject who still mourns (思慕) his predecessor; the idiomatic English makes the emperor the one mourned.

The late emperor left the empire in his hands and the infant heir in his arms; he has governed from the cradle and kept the realm at peace—work that not even the Duke of Zhou or yiyin day could surpass.
The late emperor left the empire in his hands and the infant heir in his arms; he has governed from the cradle and kept the realm at peace—work that not even the Duke of Zhou or Yi Yin could surpass.
伊尹 is the Shang minister Yi Yin; "yiyin day" is a corrupted rendering.

I beg you to heed Heaven, undertake the great work, call in high ministers and scholars, recover the classical rites, clarify the institutions of true kingship, and lead this generation into the realm of benevolence and long life—then our age could rival Cheng and Kang, and your own years those of King Wu.

I beg you to heed Heaven, undertake the great work, call in high ministers and scholars, recover the classical rites, clarify the institutions of true kingship, and lead this generation into the realm of benevolence and long life—then our age could rival Cheng and Kang, and your own years those of Gaozong.
高宗 is Gaozong (Wu Ding) of Shang, famed for his long reign, not King Wu.
In the eighth year of Emperor Cheng's reign the throne meant to give him heavier duties, named him metropolitan governor of the capital, and watched how he managed administrative business.
After eight years, Emperor Cheng meant to give him heavier duties, named him metropolitan governor of the capital, and watched how he managed administrative business.
八歲 counts eight years of Wang Jun's service, not the eighth regnal year of Emperor Cheng.

When Xue Yan left his post as governor of Left Fengyi to succeed Wang Jun as lesser-treasury superintendent, the office of imperial counselor fell vacant. Gu Yong argued, "A wise ruler does not hand out titles ahead of proven results.

When Xue Xuan left his post as governor of Left Fengyi to succeed Wang Jun as lesser-treasury superintendent, the office of imperial counselor fell vacant. Gu Yong argued, "A wise ruler does not hand out titles ahead of proven results.
薛宣 is Xue Xuan; "Yan" misreads 宣.
Xue Yan's administrative record is already on the books—use that as your measure of merit."
Xue Xuan's administrative record is already on the books—use that as your measure of merit."
薛宣 is Xue Xuan; "Yan" misreads 宣.
Within a month Xue Yan jumped from lesser treasury to imperial counselor and soon reached the chancellorship.
Within a month Xue Xuan jumped from lesser treasury to imperial counselor and soon reached the chancellorship.
薛宣 is Xue Xuan; "Yan" misreads 宣.
Wang Jun stepped into Xue Yan's former post as imperial counselor while both men still held top rank.
Wang Jun stepped into Xue Xuan's former post as imperial counselor while both men still held top rank.
薛宣 is Xue Xuan; "Yan" misreads 宣.
Months afterward Xue Yan was removed, and Zhai Fangjin became chancellor in his place.
Months afterward Xue Xuan was removed, and Zhai Fangjin became chancellor in his place.
薛宣 is Xue Xuan; "Yan" misreads 宣.
Antiquity fixed the scale of the palace: no more than nine ladies-in-waiting and eight teams of chariot horses.
Antiquity fixed the scale of the palace: no more than nine ladies-in-waiting and eight grain-fed horses.
秣馬不過八匹 counts eight horses (匹), not teams.
As grand counselor he repeatedly debated policy, filing dozens of memorials.
While in office he repeatedly debated policy, filing dozens of memorials.
自禹在位 means "after Gong Yu took office"; he was Imperial Counselor, not "grand counselor".

Today mints and iron monopolies deploy clerks, troops, and convicts to strip mountains of ore—well over a hundred thousand laborers a year. Seven commoners eat on one middle farmer's yield; that means seven hundred thousand mouths starve for every mint we run.

Today mints and iron monopolies deploy clerks, troops, and convicts to strip mountains of ore—well over a hundred thousand laborers a year. Seven commoners eat on one middle farmer's yield; so seven hundred thousand people constantly go hungry.
七十萬人常受其飢 states a fixed total going hungry; "for every mint we run" is not in the source.

He died a few months after becoming imperial counselor; the emperor gave his family a million cash, appointed his son a gentleman, who rose eventually to metropolitan commandant of the eastern commandery.
He died a few months after becoming imperial counselor; the emperor gave his family a million cash, appointed his son a gentleman, who rose eventually to Chief Commandant of Dong Commandery.
東郡都尉 is the Chief Commandant of Dong Commandery; "metropolitan" is not in the source.
Xia Hou Chang retorted, "Ritual itself allows for change."
Xiahou Chang retorted, "Ritual itself allows for change."
夏侯常 is Xiahou Chang; the surname 夏侯 should not be split.
Once Wang Mang seized the throne he sent the Five Weights commissioners on tour; they called on Gong Sheng with sheep and wine.
Once Wang Mang seized the throne he sent the Five Majesties commanders on tour; they called on Gong Sheng with sheep and wine.
五威將帥 are the "Five Majesties" commanders; "Weights" mistranslates 威.
He loved the classics and served as a village bailiff in his county, then as assistant magistrate in the Shu prefecture office.
He loved the classics and served as a village bailiff in his county, then as acting assistant magistrate of Shuzhou.
守束州丞 means acting assistant of Shuzhou county (束州), not a "Shu prefecture office".
The palace gate lies only a few dozen paces from the censor's yamen, yet for two years I could not win an audience—how much farther off are the humble petitioners of the coast!
The palace gate lies only a few dozen paces from the inner palace doors, yet for two years I could not win an audience—how much farther off are the humble petitioners of the coast!
省戶 are the doors of the inner palace apartments, not a censor's office.
He was charged with blocking imperial officers, gross disrespect, and conduct unworthy of a minister, and jailed pending execution.
He was charged with blocking imperial officers, gross disrespect, and conduct unworthy of a minister, and sent to the Commandant of Justice's prison.
下廷尉獄 means he was sent to the Commandant of Justice's prison; "pending execution" is not in the source.

When Longxi issued a warrant for Xin Xing, he stopped once at Bao Xuan's house with Xu Dan, Bao's son-in-law, shared a meal, and left; Bao Xuan knew nothing of the charge, was arrested as an accomplice, and took his own life in prison.

When Longxi issued a warrant for Xin Xing, he stopped once at Bao Xuan's house with Xu Gan, Bao's son-in-law, shared a meal, and left; Bao Xuan knew nothing of the charge, was arrested as an accomplice, and took his own life in prison.
許紺 is Xu Gan; 紺 is read gàn, not "Dan".

From Emperor Cheng to Wang Mang, noted men of integrity included Ji Qun and Wang Si of Langya, Xue Fang (Zirong) of Qi, Xun Yue and Xun Xiang of Taiyuan, and Tang Lin and Tang Zun of Pei—all famed for classical learning and upright lives.

From Emperor Cheng to Wang Mang, noted men of integrity included Ji Qun (style Wangsi) of Langya, Xue Fang (Zirong) of Qi, Xun Yue and Xun Xiang of Taiyuan, and Tang Lin and Tang Zun of Pei—all famed for classical learning and upright lives.
In 紀逡王思, 王思 is Ji Qun's courtesy name, matching the name-plus-style pattern of the other entries; it is not a second person.
